evidence: Fresh independent residue replay over the full parity period gives residues {1,5}.
correctness.rationale: Writing an even perfect number as \(2^{p-1}(2^p-1)\) and removing the common power of two from \(x,y\) reduces to positive \(u,v\) not both even. Opposite parity would make both \(u+v\) and the alternating cofactor nontrivial odd factors of the unique odd prime, impossible. Thus \(u,v\) are odd and the odd cofactor \(B_m\) must equal the Mersenne prime. For \(m=4k+1\), setting \(r\equiv uv^{-1}\pmod8\) gives \(B_m\equiv1+2k(1-r)\pmod8\), hence only 1 or 5 modulo 8, never the required 7 for \(p\ge3\). The \(p=2\) perfect number 6 is excluded directly. A fresh residue replay over the complete odd residue classes reproduced only \(\{1,5\}\); the infinite conclusion rests on the symbolic formula, not the finite replay.
